newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says Swiss CPI overstates inflation.
newsitem.headline: SNB says Swiss CPI overstates inflation.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) president Hans Meyer on Wednesday reiterated comments by SNB officials that the Swiss consumer price index (CPI) overstates inflation.
The January CPI is due for release Friday. In December, year-on-year inflation was measured at 0.8 percent. Swiss economists expect a rise in January of 0.6 to 0.7 percent.

"The average yearly inflation measured by the index of consumer prices was 0.8 percent last year. We have thus practically reached the goal of price stability," Meyer said in the text of a speech to a regional economic group.
"We tolerate a slight increase in the price level, because the consumer price index overstates inflation," Meyer said.
"If we were to aim for zero inflation, the effective price level would decline," he said.
He said improvements in the quality of goods which are measured by the CPI, as well as new products and a tendency by consumers to buy cheaper goods had led to the overstating.
"These developments are not sufficiently measured in the basket of goods which is used to compile the CPI," he said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
